subject: Request: Contractual exit remedies & conditional fee-at-risk (Atlas Health)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlashealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: exit remedies & penalties for SLA breaches

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the recent demo — the platform looks promising. Procurement asked me to confirm a few legal items before we proceed to signature. Specifically, Atlas has a hard requirement for remedies that go beyond service credits in the event of repeated or material SLA failures for regulated workloads:

- The ability to terminate for repeated unremedied availability or latency SLO breaches (we're thinking 3 incidents in a rolling 90-day window).
- A cash-at-risk escrow equal to 3 months of committed fees in the event of a termination for SLA cause, to cover transition costs.
- A liquidated-damages schedule for catastrophic outages (defined in our draft as >24 continuous hours outage impacting >50% of production requests) capped at the equivalent of 6 months' committed fees.

We know these are stronger than typical vendor language; Atlas is regulated and their risk committee requires these levers for any vendor serving PHI-adjacent workflows. Can you confirm whether Redwood would consider these remedies? If not, please propose alternative protections (e.g., expanded credits plus contractual transition assistance) that would be acceptable to Atlas.

Attached is a short impact memo from our ops team that explains the expected business impact and estimated failover cost.

Would appreciate a written position so I can share with procurement/legal tomorrow.

Thanks,
Liam

Attachment: SLA_impact_analysis_Q2.pdf (PDF, 210KB)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: exit remedies & penalties for SLA breaches

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear note and for sharing Atlas's requirements. I discussed this with our legal and commercial teams. Short answer: Redwood is open to stronger operational commitments, but we need to balance customer risk and our platform-level SLAs with standard limitations on liability.

Outlined below is our initial position and a couple of options we can offer for Atlas to discuss internally:

Option A — Standard credits + enhanced support (preferred):
- 99.9% monthly uptime SLO for the contracted services; credits up to 100% of monthly fees for a severe monthly breach.
- Incident response SLA + dedicated escalation contacts and playbook.
- Transition assistance: 60 days of free dedicated onboarding engineering and expedited data export APIs.
- No contract termination right tied solely to credits.

Option B — Conditional fee-at-risk (limited, by exception):
- We can consider a capped fee-at-risk escrow (held in trust) equal to up to 3 months of committed fees but only under a narrow definition of repeated, unremedied breaches with objective metrics and remediation windows.
- Any liquidation of escrow funds would require an agreed process: notice, 30-day remediation window, third-party verification of severity.
- Cap on aggregate liquidated damages at 6 months' fees.

We cannot accept uncapped liquidated damages or immediate termination solely on the basis of a single incident. If Atlas would like to pursue Option B, we would need your procurement and legal teams to provide: the specific incident metrics you intend to apply, the remediation timelines you expect, and any required third-party audit language.

I'll loop in our commercial lead (Marissa) and legal handler (Karthik) so we can produce proposed contract language. If it helps, we can also provide a redlined draft that inserts conditional escrow and a short verification workflow.

Best,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: exit remedies & penalties for SLA breaches

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Atlas procurement note. They asked for termination rights + escrow/liquidated damages. See Liam's attached impact memo.

Quick thoughts:
- This is higher-risk language than our standard terms. We can offer the conditional escrow (Option B) but we need firm limits and a verification path to avoid disputes.
- Suggest we propose a remediation ladder: notice -> 30 days to fix -> independent verification (one-time, mutually agreed vendor) -> release or liquidation limited to three months fees, six-month cap aggregate. Also propose a mutual right to cure for Redwood.
- Marissa: can you estimate commercial exposure if we agreed to a 3-month escrow + 6-month aggregate cap for their committed tier? We should show them numbers and a fallback credit-only option.
- Karthik: legal will need to craft language that ties termination rights to documented failure to meet SLOs for 3 incidents in 90 days OR a catastrophic outage definition. Avoid per-incident immediate termination. Also, we should insist on a joint runbook and 3rd-party verification clause.

Can we aim to get a redlined clause back to them by end of week? I attached a starter draft.

Thanks,
Soojin

Attachment: redwood-draft_SLA_clauses.docx (DOCX, 45KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlashealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: exit remedies & penalties for SLA breaches

Hi Liam — thanks for the detailed ask and for the impact memo. We reviewed internally and want to propose the following compromise that preserves Atlas's risk controls while also protecting Redwood from open-ended liability:

Counterproposal (Redwood):
1) Termination for cause: Atlas may terminate for SLA cause where the following have occurred within a rolling 90-day window: (a) three separate monthly SLO breaches as defined in Section 1.2; or (b) a single catastrophic outage (continuous >24 hours affecting >=50% production traffic) that Redwood fails to remediate despite the agreed runbook.

2) Conditional escrow: Redwood agrees to place a mutually agreed escrow equal to 3 months of Atlas's committed monthly fees upon mutual execution of the contract. The escrow will be governed by a simple trust agreement; release of funds requires: (i) formal notice of breach; (ii) Redwood provided 30 days to remedy; and (iii) independent verification by a mutually selected third-party monitoring firm confirming the breach and inability to remedy.

3) Liquidated damages cap: Aggregate LGD that may be recovered from escrow or by contractor action shall not exceed 6 months of committed fees.

4) Transition assistance: If Atlas terminates for SLA cause, Redwood will provide up to 90 days of transition assistance (remote engineer hours and prioritized support) plus export of data via our standard APIs.

5) Optional: If Atlas requires a faster remediation window for certain regulated workloads, we can add a separate SLO tier with a reduced remediation window and a commensurate increase in committed fees.

Next steps: if Atlas is comfortable with the language above, we can produce a redline for the Master Services Agreement and the escrow trust agreement. Otherwise, please indicate which pieces are deal-breakers for you so we can prioritize.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0243

Marissa attached a draft runbook and a sample escrow trust exhibit for reference.
